title: Emrys and the Garden
premise: Elodie Delacroix, cartographer of unmapped realms, keeps the ledgers of the Guild of Impossible Things—until a boy named Emrys arrives at her door speaking a language older than kingdoms and carrying a map that redraws itself. The map leads to King Aldous Vey, whose crown has been slowly replaced by a living thing called the Verdant Writ, which grants wishes by consuming memories. As Elodie teaches Emrys modern speech, she discovers he is not a messenger but a fragment of the king's stolen childhood, sent back as a warning. To unbind Aldous, Elodie must choose between the guild's law of neutrality and the truth she owes Emrys—and in the end she burns the ledgers, frees the king at the cost of her own mapped identity, and plants a garden where the guild once stood.
about_author: E. M. Delacroix is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing maps of places that no longer exist. They write fantasy about people who keep records of things better left forgotten.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Impossibilities
chapters.summary: POV Elodie. A night of routine bookkeeping in the Guild of Impossible Things establishes its rules: record everything, trade fairly, never intervene. Elodie catalogs a bottled echo and a debt paid in shadows. Emotional beat: quiet competence masking loneliness, as she realizes every entry is someone else's story but none are hers.

chapters.title: A Knock Older Than Kingdoms
chapters.summary: POV Elodie. A child appears at the guild door at midnight, soaked in rain that hasn't fallen yet, speaking a language no ledger records. He carries a folded map that shifts when unobserved. Emotional beat: wonder sharpened into unease—the guild's bells ring for him though he was never traded for.

chapters.title: Emrys
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. Inside the boy's mind, the world is noise and half-remembered sunlight; he knows only that he must deliver the map to 'the one who draws what isn't there.' He recognizes Elodie instantly. Emotional beat: disorientation and fierce, inexplicable trust—he has been walking toward her longer than he can count.

chapters.title: The Cartographer's Oath
chapters.summary: POV Elodie. Guildmaster Corvane orders the boy logged as an anomaly and the map confiscated. Elodie resists, citing the oath that all arrivals be mapped before claimed. She begins teaching Emrys common speech through drawings. Emotional beat: first rebellion—a small act of loyalty against an institution she has served faithfully.

chapters.title: What the Map Draws Back
chapters.summary: POV Elodie. Studying the shifting map, Elodie finds it depicts the capital with a garden growing through the palace—garden paths spelling words in Emrys's dead language. The map redraws itself each time she sleeps. Emotional beat: dread blooming into obsession; the map is not describing a place, it's remembering one.

chapters.title: Lessons in Borrowed Words
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. Emrys learns speech quickly, too quickly, absorbing words like roots taking water. He tells Elodie fragments: a king, a crown of green, a promise made in a garden. Emotional beat: tenderness between teacher and student shadowed by his terror whenever anyone mentions the palace.

chapters.title: The Guild's Third Law
chapters.summary: POV Elodie. Corvane reveals the third law: anomalies that cannot be classified must be traded or destroyed. A buyer already waits—an emissary from the palace offering a fortune for 'the foundling.' Emotional beat: betrayal; Elodie realizes the guild knew something about Emrys before he ever arrived.

chapters.title: The Emissary Wears Grey
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. The palace emissary visits, and Emrys hides—but hearing the man's voice triggers a memory flood: this voice once sang him lullabies. The emissary leaves a sealed writ bearing the royal seal, grown over with moss. Emotional beat: recognition curdling into horror; the past is hunting him politely.

chapters.title: Flight Along Unmapped Roads
chapters.summary: POV Elodie. Rather than surrender Emrys, Elodie flees with him using a cartographer's trick: roads that exist only while drawn. They travel toward the capital ahead of the guild's hunters. Emotional beat: exhilaration and guilt—she has broken every rule she lived by, and it feels like waking up.

chapters.title: The Village That Forgot Its Name
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. They shelter in a village where no one remembers their own names, only their trades—all victims of the Verdant Writ's hunger spreading outward from the palace. Emrys unknowingly restores a baker's memory by singing. Emotional beat: hope and responsibility; the boy is not just a warning, he's an antidote.

chapters.title: Corvane Catches Up
chapters.summary: POV Elodie. Guild hunters corner them; Corvane himself arrives, and instead of force, offers truth: Emrys was created by the guild two hundred years ago as a failsafe against the Writ, then lost. Emotional beat: vertigo—her loyalty to the guild and to the boy were never opposites; both point at the same failure.

chapters.title: Two Hundred Years of Winter
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. By firelight, Corvane tells the history: King Aldous wished to end a famine, and the Writ granted it by eating the kingdom's memories, then began eating the king. The guild made Emrys from the king's stolen childhood and hid him beyond time. Emotional beat: grief for a childhood that was never lived, given purpose at last.

chapters.title: The Price of the Gate
chapters.summary: POV Elodie. The only way into the palace's heart is a door that opens for a true name freely given. Elodie realizes Emrys's true name is the king's own—speaking it will begin unbinding the Writ but may erase Emrys as a separate self. Emotional beat: the theme crystallizes; telling the truth may destroy the person she's come to love.

chapters.title: What I Would Keep
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. On the eve of the assault, Emrys asks Elodie to write down everything about their journey so some version of him might remember. They fill a small notebook together—his first possession, his first story. Emotional beat: bittersweet intimacy; he chooses truth over survival, teaching her the choice she must make.

chapters.title: The Garden in the Walls
chapters.summary: POV Elodie. They breach the palace via the map's hidden paths and find corridors strangled in flowering vines, courtiers smiling with vacant eyes. The throne room doors open onto a garden where a king sits crowned in living green. Emotional beat: awe turned sickening—the wish fulfilled is beautiful, and that is the trap.

chapters.title: Audience with the Verdant King
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. Emrys approaches Aldous, who half-wakes and mistakes him for the son he never had. The Writ speaks through the king, offering Elodie anything—her own lost history restored—if they leave. Emotional beat: temptation laid bare; the Writ weaponizes belonging itself.

chapters.title: The Ledgers Burn
chapters.summary: POV Elodie. Cornered by the Writ's bargain, Elodie understands the guild's neutrality was complicity. She burns her ledger pages in the garden's soil, declaring the truth aloud: the famine ended, but the kingdom was the price. Each spoken truth wilts part of the Writ. Emotional beat: catharsis—truth as an act of loyalty, not betrayal.

chapters.title: Emrys, Unbound
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. Emrys speaks his true name—Aldous's own—and the Writ tears free, flooding him with two centuries of the king's stolen years. He begins dissolving into light even as the king wakes whole. Emotional beat: sacrifice at full cost; he smiles because he finally belongs somewhere, even if only for a moment.

chapters.title: The King Who Remembered
chapters.summary: POV Elodie. Aldous rises, restored, and holds the fading Emrys; the Writ crumbles to seed. But the notebook survives, and Elodie reads their journey aloud to give the dying boy back his own story. Emotional beat: mourning braided with gratitude—memory given freely outlasts memory taken.

chapters.title: Where the Garden Ends
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. In dissolution, Emrys does not vanish entirely: the village-folk he healed arrive, their returned memories anchoring him. He becomes neither boy nor king but a new self, rooted in everyone who remembers him. Emotional beat: rebirth—identity as something woven from others rather than held alone.

chapters.title: A New Kind of Map
chapters.summary: POV Elodie. Months later, the guild reopens under new laws: nothing traded that cannot be told truthfully. Elodie drafts a new kind of map—not of territory but of stories, beginning with Emrys's. Emotional beat: quiet resolution; she has found belonging not in the institution but in the work remade.

chapters.title: Emrys and the Garden
chapters.summary: POV shared. Spring comes to the capital; the palace garden now grows ordinary roses. Emrys, changed and learning to be himself, tends it alongside Elodie, who is writing a book no ledger could hold. Emotional beat: peace earned—identity chosen, loyalty kept, and truth planted like a seed that finally gets to grow.
